Extract environmental values along tracks and lines

Source: R/extract_to_track.R
extract_to_track.Rd

Sample ordered trajectories and reuse extract_to_point() for environmental selection. Return sampled positions and optional summaries per track.

Usage

extract_to_track(
  data,
  nc,
  var = NULL,
  track_col = NULL,
  sampling = NULL,
  spacing_km = NULL,
  interpolate_depth = FALSE,
  interpolate_time = FALSE,
  depth_step_m = NULL,
  time_step_seconds = NULL,
  method = NULL,
  statistics = "mean",
  weighting = c("distance", "duration", "equal"),
  min_valid_fraction = 0.8,
  lon_col = "lon",
  lat_col = "lat",
  depth_col = "depth",
  date_col = "date",
  output_col = NULL,
  time_resolution = c("auto", "datetime", "daily", "monthly", "yearly", "custom"),
  max_samples = 100000L,
  max_segment_km = NULL,
  max_gap_hours = NULL,
  quiet = FALSE,
  time_step = NULL,
  time_unit = c("hours", "minutes", "seconds", "days", "months", "years"),
  land_mask = NULL,
  marine_values = NULL,
  mask_type = c("land", "marine"),
  mask_domain = NULL,
  land_policy = c("skip", "error"),
  mask_step_km = 0.5,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

Ordered vertex table: a data frame, matrix, named list or sf POINT features, as for extract_to_point(). Rows are traversed in their supplied order within each track; they are never sorted by date. Convert sf LINESTRING features first, e.g. with as.data.frame(sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_transform(lines, 4326))) and lon_col = "X", lat_col = "Y", track_col = "L1".

nc, var

netCDF sources and selected variable names. See extract_to_buffer().

track_col

Optional track identifier column. Without it, the input is one track. IDs are returned as text.

sampling

NULL (default) uses 'balanced' when spacing_km, depth_step_m, time_step_seconds or time_step is supplied, and 'vertices' otherwise. 'vertices' uses observations only; 'balanced' uses a shared subdivision satisfying all explicit step limits; 'merged_steps' combines distance/depth cuts with temporal cuts; 'cells' splits each connection at grid boundaries and samples interval midpoints, retaining original vertices. Repeated visits are retained. Cells mode currently uses spatial within matching.

spacing_km

Maximum horizontal spacing in kilometres when inserting samples. Supply spacing or another step explicitly for balanced or merged_steps.

interpolate_depth, interpolate_time

Allow linear interpolation of depth and elapsed UTC time between vertices. FALSE by default. Constant endpoint values are retained; missing endpoints produce missing intermediate values.

depth_step_m, time_step_seconds

Optional maximum changes between samples. Require the corresponding interpolation switch. They supplement horizontal spacing, including for stationary or vertically moving tracks.

method

Depth method passed to extract_to_point(), including 'all'. NULL uses nearest for variables with depth and 2d for variables without it.

statistics

NULL for samples only, or distinct names from mean, sd, se, min and max. Summaries describe sampled environmental selections.

weighting

'distance', 'duration' or 'equal'. Distance and duration assign half each adjacent segment's horizontal length or elapsed seconds to its endpoint samples. Equal gives each sample the same weight.

min_valid_fraction

Minimum valid fraction of total requested track support for a summary, from zero to one. Missing values stay in its denominator.

lon_col, lat_col, depth_col, date_col

Vertex coordinate columns. Dates are required for selected temporal variables, duration weights or time-gap limits.

output_col

Output name or named variable-to-column mapping.

time_resolution

Point-time precision; see extract_to_point(). With auto, the original observations determine precision, before interpolation.

max_samples

Maximum total sampled positions, a positive integer.

max_segment_km, max_gap_hours

Optional limits that reject long segments or known elapsed time gaps. Split disconnected trajectories explicitly. FALSE by default because geometric elevation may use a different convention.

quiet

Hide explanatory reports; scientific and time-zone warnings remain.

time_step, time_unit

Optional temporal step and units: seconds, minutes, hours, elapsed days, whole calendar months or years. Balanced sampling uses one equal subdivision per original segment for elapsed-time limits. Calendar steps advance from each preceding step in UTC, clamping to the destination month's end. Balanced sampling preserves these calendar anchors and subdivides each calendar span to satisfy distance/depth limits.

land_mask

Optional sf polygon or single-layer terra SpatRaster mask. With no mask, marine connectivity is not checked. Geographic rasters must use longitudes from -180 to 180; rotate or reproject other conventions explicitly. Antimeridian connections are split.

marine_values

Numeric raster codes representing marine cells, including the underlying codes of categorical rasters.

mask_type

Meaning of polygon interiors: land or marine.

mask_domain

Optional polygon domain for polygon masks. A land polygon alone cannot establish that its exterior is known sea. For rasters, coverage is defined by their extent and missing cells.

land_policy

Skip invalid connections (default) or raise an error. Original observations remain; invalid support stays in the denominator.

mask_step_km

Maximum segment length of the polyline used for mask predicates. This is an approximation to the geodesic; coastline accuracy also depends on the supplied mask. Touching land counts as an intersection.

...

Point-selection options: file_col, dimension overrides, time_match, max_time_diff, custom_time_interval, spatial_match, max_distance_km, and time_report, spatial_report, depth_report, verbose.

Value

A list with samples (coordinates, original vertex attributes, source-row references, sample support and extracted values), summary (one row per track and output, or NULL), and settings. Tracks follow first appearance order. Summary counts n_observed and n_assumed distinguish original vertices from inserted positions; n_samples is their total, including missing results and invalid connections. The same counts are available once per track in settings$sampling_counts, even when statistics = NULL. Cell-interval midpoints count as assumed positions. variation_status is not_requested when neither SD nor SE is requested, available when the requested variation statistics are finite, or insufficient_variation_samples when accepted support has fewer than two valid samples. not_available covers rejected support or non-finite statistics; consult status for coverage and support problems. status follows extract_to_buffer(): empty (no known support), all_missing, insufficient_coverage, partial or complete. Samples follow traversal order. For vertices-only sampling the global input row order is retained. Non-coordinate attributes of inserted samples are NA. source_row indexes the input rows.

Interpretation and limits

Positions follow WGS84 shortest geodesics. Distances are horizontal, not three-dimensional travel distances. Antipodal endpoints need a waypoint. Interpolated coordinates describe assumptions, not observations.

Balanced sampling approximates line integration. Cells mode finds numerical intersections with rectilinear spatial cell boundaries and selection changes in depth and time. It retains separate segment visits, including returns to the same cell. Zero-support original vertices remain available for inspection. Cells mode is not a volume-weighted integration of physical averaging periods; the temporal rules still compare timestamp labels. Custom temporal precision and spatial nearest matching are currently unsupported in cells mode. Overlapping sources with different horizontal grids require explicit alignment or another sampling mode. Environmental values are selected using extract_to_point(), never interpolated. Missing coordinates are rejected and multipart lines must be split explicitly.

SD and SE use the same reliability-weight correction and effective sample size as extract_to_buffer(). Adjacent samples are usually correlated: SE is descriptive under an independence assumption, not an uncertainty estimate. Densifying a track does not create independent environmental observations. Distance-weighted summaries of stationary tracks are NA; duration weighting requires known time support and returns NA if any adjacent duration is unknown. settings records options and candidate files. Actual selected records are stored in the per-output match_info columns in samples.

See also

extract_to_point(), extract_to_buffer()

Examples

nc_file <- system.file("extdata", "example_2d.nc", package = "ocean3d")
track <- data.frame(
  lon = c(0, 1), lat = c(40, 40),
  date = as.Date(c("2020-01-01", "2020-01-01"))
)
result <- extract_to_track(track, nc_file,
  var = "temp", method = "2d",
  spacing_km = 20, quiet = TRUE
)
result$summary
#>   track_id output_column weighting n_samples n_observed n_assumed n_valid
#> 1        1          temp  distance         6          2         4       6
#>   valid_fraction total_distance_km total_duration_seconds effective_n   status
#> 1              1          85.39341                      0    5.555556 complete
#>   mean variation_status
#> 1 15.5    not_requested
